content:
A website is not finished at launch. Plugins release security fixes, PHP versions reach end of life, SSL certificates need renewing, forms stop sending email after a hosting change, and pages slowly get heavier as new images are added. None of this is visible until something breaks, often at the worst time: during a property launch, an admissions season or a sale. We look after business websites for Gurugram companies from our Sohna Road office, and this page explains what regular maintenance involves and whether you need it.

Signs your website needs attention now

  • Your WordPress dashboard shows a long list of pending updates.
  • Enquiries have dropped, and nobody has checked whether the contact form still works.
  • The site takes several seconds to load on a phone.
  • Google Search Console reports errors, or you have never set it up.
  • You do not know when the last backup was taken, or where it is stored.
  • Your browser shows a "Not secure" warning, or the SSL certificate expired once before.
  • The person who built the site has moved on and nobody has the logins.

What a maintenance plan covers

The exact list depends on your platform, but a typical plan follows this routine.

Every week

  • Core, theme and plugin updates, tested on a staging copy first for sites that take payments or bookings.
  • Malware and file-change scans.
  • Uptime monitoring, with alerts to us if the site goes down.
  • Test submission of your main enquiry form.

Every month

  • Backup check: confirm daily off-site backups are running, and do a test restore to staging from time to time.
  • PageSpeed and Core Web Vitals check on key pages, with fixes for new problems such as oversized images.
  • Broken link and 404 error review in Search Console.
  • Small content changes within the plan's allowance: updating prices, team members, timings or banners.
  • A short plain-English report of what was done and anything that needs a decision from you.

Every quarter

  • Review of user accounts, removing ex-employees and agencies who no longer need access.
  • PHP version and hosting health check, including disk space and email deliverability.
  • Domain and SSL renewal dates confirmed, so nothing lapses.
  • Plugin and app review, removing anything unused.

Platforms we maintain

  • WordPress
  • WooCommerce
  • Shopify
  • Custom PHP sites
  • Static HTML sites
  • cPanel and Hostinger hosting
  • VPS and cloud servers

Shopify stores need less technical upkeep because Shopify handles hosting and security, so maintenance there focuses on apps, theme updates, speed and content.

The first month: a health audit

We do not take over a site blind. Every plan begins with an audit that usually takes one to two weeks:

  1. Access and ownership check. We confirm the domain, hosting and Google accounts are in your company's name, and help recover any that are not.
  2. Full backup taken before we touch anything.
  3. Security scan for malware, outdated software, unknown admin users and nulled plugins.
  4. Speed and SEO baseline recorded, so later reports compare against real starting numbers.
  5. Fix list shared with you, separating urgent problems from things that can wait.

Access we need from you

An administrator login for the website, hosting control panel access (or a hosting account where we can be added as a user), DNS access at your domain registrar, and Search Console and Analytics access for your Google account. We use a password manager, and all access is returned or removed if you end the plan.

What is not part of routine maintenance

New pages beyond the plan's allowance, redesigns, new features, integrations and large content projects are quoted separately. So is cleaning a site that was already hacked before the plan started, because that work varies a lot. We tell you before any extra work begins, never after.

If your site is hacked or down today

We first take a copy of the infected site for investigation, then restore a clean backup if one exists, or clean the files and database by hand if not. We then find how the attacker got in, change every password, remove the weakness, and request a review in Google Search Console if Google flagged the site. After that, regular maintenance is what keeps it from happening again.

When a maintenance plan is not worth it

If you have a static site that rarely changes, an in-house developer who already handles updates, or a Shopify store your team manages comfortably, a monthly plan may not add much. A yearly check-up may be enough, and we are happy to say so.

How plans are priced

Cost depends on the platform, the number of plugins or apps, whether the site takes payments, how much content work you need each month, and the response time you want. We quote a fixed monthly or annual fee after a free consultation and an initial look at your site.

Maintenance FAQs

Can you maintain a site that another agency built?

Yes. Most sites we maintain were built by someone else. The first-month audit is how we learn the site and find any hidden problems.

Will updates break my website?

They can, which is why we test updates on a staging copy for important sites and always take a backup first. If something still breaks, we roll back and fix it.

How quickly do you respond if the site goes down?

Response times are written into your plan. Uptime monitoring alerts us directly, so we often know before you do.

Do you also handle hosting renewals and business email?

We track renewal dates and can manage hosting for you, but the accounts stay in your company's name and billing stays with you.

Can we cancel the plan?

Yes. On cancellation we hand over all logins, the latest backups and a note on the site's current state.

Many of the sites we look after were built years ago, some still listing an old Gurgaon address. Wherever yours stands, meet us at Tower B1, Spaze I-Tech Park, Sohna Road, Sector 49, or book a free consultation and share your site link. We will point out the most urgent issues before you decide on anything.
